 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Any hopes of Davante Adams returning to face his former team on Thanksgiving Eve appear to be fading.
 Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay poured cold water on speculation that his star wide receiver could return from a hamstring injury for Wednesday night's primetime showdown against the Green Bay Packers.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Don't think he's ready quite yet," McVay told reporters Monday morning. "There is a possibility he'll be ready the game after the Packers."
 That game would be Thursday, December 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs at SoFi Stadium.
 Adams ruptured his hamstring against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6 and was placed on injured reserve. He underwent surgery to "clean up" the hamstring and was expected to miss between 6 and 10 weeks.
 It's another tough break for the Rams, who are already without Puka Nacua following knee surgery, leaving Matthew Stafford dangerously thin at wide receiver for one of the biggest games of their season.
